chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) if a man missed one of the takbirs, or two, or three, he said: 'He should takbir for what he missed.'

key_terms.يُكَبِّرُ مَا فَاتَهُ: He takbirs for what he missed

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they join the funeral prayer late and miss some of the takbirs?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of joining the congregational funeral prayer, establishing that the latecomer's obligation is limited to the specific takbirs missed rather than repeating the entire prayer. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus on the modular nature of Salat al-Janazah, where each takbir serves a distinct supplicatory function, ensuring the validity of the prayer even when entered late. It underscores the practical flexibility in communal worship, allowing individuals to fulfill their duty without disrupting the flow of the congregation.
